Built the five Chronicle core navigation modules under `design/visual-lab/src/core/`, verified against §4.1–4.6 and §6.5 of the architecture doc, and confirmed with a throwaway smoke test (since removed) before running the real gate:

- **`scope.ts`** — regex-based parse/format for the four path forms; ancestor-slug requirement falls out of the regex structure itself (a campaign can't parse without `/u/<universe>` present).
- **`objectRef.ts`** — canonical text form is `type:id` only, never slug; `sameObject` compares type+id+scope, ignoring revision.
- **`viewRecipe.ts`** — exact lookup table from the brief's required mappings; also exports a runtime `RECIPE_IDS` array (used by `deepLink.ts` for validation) since the required exports only give a type, not a runtime list.
- **`visibility.ts`** — `public` always resolves to `not_found`; GM tier is a `Set` membership check, never a numeric rank; `secret` is `not_found` for everyone else (never `redacted`, per the "confirms existence" rule).
- **`deepLink.ts`** — reuses `formatScope` for the scope prefix, adds workspace segments (`world`/`prepare`/`table`/`forge`), and picks between two object encodings: the pretty `/world/objects/<slug>` path (only when there's no recipe/focus riding along, since that path form can't carry the object's `type`) versus a `<type>=<slug>` query pair everywhere else — which is what actually round-trips object+recipe together, per the brief's explicit requirement.

One judgment call worth flagging: the pretty `objects/<slug>` path form has no room to encode an object's `type` in the URL, so `parseDeepLink` assigns it the placeholder type `"object"` — documented inline. Everywhere a recipe or focus is also present, the object goes through the query-param form instead, which preserves the real type exactly.

`npm --prefix design/visual-lab run build` passes clean (`tsc --noEmit && vite build`), and `git status` shows only the new `src/core/` directory — no other files touched.
